content: The Sapper is a Proud Military Airship, serving in the last war against the filthy French invaders. It has been decommissioned as a military vessel although it's heritage is shown. The Union Jack fly's proudly from it's mast
With a freshly painted owl on the bow
There is a verrrrry old pigeon here. Thats all. Its just old.

*Captians Log, Day 1 in the Empire City. At last I am home, however the rumors of change have surely been proven true. I have yet to see the bustle of the city during the day yet I can already see the effects come nightfall. After three days up at mast I unfortunately was all knackered up after unloading the cargo. I feel quite embarrassed but life has a peculiar way of getting lively even at night. I took a night time jaunt through the Hamstead on my way to Central Park, it seemed better than doing bugger all back at my ship, and while I was going through what I thought was going to be an empty street like I remembered from my youth I was greet by a small ruckus in the distance. Deciding to just pass through I couldn't help but shake a strong feeling of unease as not only when entered the burrough the feeling left as soon as I had taken leave of it. The streets were being patrolled by soldiers to find people breaking curfew and walking about when there not supposed to, and I have more than a few inklings of an idea why. The people here are not all to fond of the occupation here and may try to take action, but the streets of Hamstead are not safe. There's rumor of folk missing. The French siege was but a year ago, the wounds I saw were still scarred over and there may still be sympathizers left. I wish the people would understand that it's only a ploy to undermine the strength of the crown, yet I digress for now. 
More peculiar though tonight I received a sign from the Gods, Along my way through central park I stumbled into a dreamlike event. A BLOODY UNICORN AND LION! By the gods and kings might I was about to let the blessed creature be killed by the Lion, yet i was reluctant to take the beast out myself. In the end I was forced to as the beast turned on me and I was unable to scare it off. It nearly took me out as well.*

*Forced into a rough position I poured everything I had into slaying it, although I was in mine own folly unarmed. To my despair both beasts had perished that night, as the Unicorn had used the last of it's strength to save me. I waited with it to meet the pale one and comfort it in it's last moments. When it had moved on I performed funeral rites for both. I plan on visiting again the following tomorrow as I have a strong feeling that even though both beasts had passed things were not laid to rest as one might say. I look forward to tomorrow in light of these events. Maybe I can do something to help the good people of Hamstead.*1

*Captains log, Day 2. Today has become a right mess and I don't have a single clue as to what to make of it, My early day was uneventful as I spent hours looking for the ol'quarter but for the life of me I couldn't make heads or tails, and the usual in-climate weather was heralded by a burst of thunder. Then I was out in the breeze with the events in Central Park as well. The night didn't get all buggered up until I tried to return home in the evn'n. I was on walk-about through Hamstead when I came across two soldiers getting the weapons knicked off of them by another vet (to my best guess a Sargent) trying to give them all frazzled for sleeping on the watch. I was shocked to discover after waking them that they had no respect for those that have come before them, and they tried to arrest me. Another bloke came around off the docks and tried to get them off me by gettin them to chase him instead. He called out saying "If you want to catch a real crook come after me instead." It was a clever ruse if I must say so meself but I lost track of the quickly. A little later one I found out that the Sargent who knicked the swords off of them was keepin and eye in the sky, at that the Bloke had been caught. I quickly came after him because I believe in keeping things square, and it ended up with the two guards dead. What's worse is that the Man is French! What was I doing I hate the French! They've given us nothing but war and revolution for the past 700 years! I never would have thought that I would help one of the wine guzzling ninnies, But I also never thought that a Frenchman would ever save me from arrest. I'm at a loss for what I should do now, Maybe it's the fog or something but Something is definitely all buggered up here. I Know the crown won't forgive me for what's happened but I tried to stick to my code as best as I can*

Luard approached the airship carefully. "Hello, is one Johnathan Wrask here?"
(taking a long rest i think)
(actually my ship was supposed to be out of port, I'm at work right now but if you could give me a couple of minutes I can take a short break)
(I forgot to enter that into everything but that's what I'll have to do)
(okok, I can wait! you can focus on your work for now)
(I'm up for lunch break)
"Oh, hello there, what can I do you for?"

Luard bows politely as a greeting. "The name is Luard Dragonheart, writer for the Empire Post. I'm here to ask you about your fight with the Redcoats this morning." Learning from his interaction with Eldon, Luard lowers his voice so that people won't hear. "Can I ask for a statement from you?"
Johnathan's face grows pale,"Come now, come in quickly"

Luard walks in the ship. He notices Johnathan's pale face, "Don't worry friend" He says with a smile. "I'm not here to arrest you, if anything, I'm on your side actually, I too have a bone to pick with the redcoats."

Papers are scattered everywhere, there is a dragon chess board with scribbles all over it. "I don't know what you're talking about, I'm loyal to my king and country and I haven't done anything to jeopardize that!"
(he's a terrible liar so I don't want to roll deception in case it turns out well)

"I am not here to investigate nor aprrehend. The Empire Post is sympathetic to you rebels, going off of what our opinion pieces say." Luard reaffirms with a gentle smile. "I'm just here to ask for a simple statement. Eldon already gave me his account, recruitment and everything. I just want everyone's messages to be let out to the masses, is all."

"That damned Frenchman, Oh how could everything go so wrong. I was just trying to give them a scare and make sure they weren't going to sleep on watch again! I'm a veteran, I know that ends up with people dead. But they wouldn't listen to me, mocked me even"
He collapses into a chair next to the table with the chess board, there is another across from him as well

Luard's eyes glint with the prospect of yet another angle to this growing story. "So you do not like what the patriots are doing?" He inquires to continue Johnathan's story along, sitting on the chair across the half-orc.

"More like the traitors and French loyalists! At least that's what I used to think. Sure occupation is tough but they're just supposed to be keeping everyone safe. Last night I was walking home past curfew, and I stumble into the sleep guards! Another person who I believe to also be a veteran was knicking their supplies as tradition usually follows to hide them. So I woke them up after she left to scare their knockers off. They decide to arrest me and that's when I another man comes out and tries to draw them away from me. I didn't want him to risk his skin over me so I stayed close once he gave them the slip"
(He's entirely reliable when it comes to appraising other people)
Luard nods at all of this juicy new information. "This exactly what I needed thank you. The patriots have given me their message, do you have one you want printed on the paper?"

"I didn't have a choice! They had taken him down and I'm not about to let another person suffer for my decisions. I did what I had to do to save repay him, how was I supposed to know that he was french! I just want people to know that we must stand strong together for the good of the people"
"please don't let them know my name, I couldn't live with the shame"

"You have my guarantee that you shall remain anonymous." Luard nods at what Johnathan says. "And what do you have to say about the redcoats? What with them harrassing people on the street and bombing the city."
(If you want his journal is sitting out if you want to copy information from there as well)
"They're supposed to protect us, how will the people never grow to trust them if they treat the people and the city like an invaded city"
"I know that the people here don't make it easy but they have to try"

"It is refreshing to hear a truly objective stance in this issue. You are not obsessively patriotic nor are you obsessively a crown loyalist. In it for the people I see. I respect your principles Mr. Wrask." Luard says while bowing his head, his words genuine. "I am grateful for your help, this is more than enough information for an article." Luard then steps up to leave before stopping. "For my last question," He says in his place, his tone eager, "If you met the *frenchman* once more, what would you say to him?"
"I don't know what I'd have to say, he saved me and I saved him. In many ways I wish I hadn't but he knew who I was before he chose to save me, so in many ways I feel like I owe him more"

"Interesting." Luard says with a smirk, Johnathan was breaking any and all expectations Luard had. "I'll be going now Mr. Wrask, you may look forward to reading the Empire Post article for the 14th. I'll be going now." Luard said as he walked out the ship and out of Johnathan's field of view. He heads for his airship, the <#863618958863237140>, to write his article.
Exhausted, Johnathan will go back to playing dragonchess

*Captain's Log, Day 3. Today has been quite tumultuous for me indeed. I'm still recouping from my actions the night prior and they appear to have come up to me. That blasted Frenchman had told a reporter that I had slain the two soldiers, however the reporter had not seem perturbed by it in the slightest. In fact they were quite excited by it, a most disturbing thought, it shows evidence for something that i was beginning to fear. The people here are on the cusp of treason, rebellion, and anarchy! Yet who is to blame I am not quite so certain. The army has been bombing area's of the main city and the occupation of Hamstead has grown quite violent. I fear that the crown does not know what is truly going on here. Normally the moral lines fit rather neatly into good and bad, and with my Goddess's guidance and the King's wisdom I have normally been able to see those lines clearly. However all I am able to find here are shades of grey where black and white once where. Other than that incident I spent most of my day writing reading my old journals, talking to myself, saluting the flag and play dragon chess. The most peculiar part for me was that I was unable to finish any match beyond a draw. My heart seems to be racked with guilt and uncertainty. I feel I must do something to make things better here, but I don't know If I can do it alone. Maybe I try to find a pilot?*

Luard enters the familiar airship and leaves a note saying:
     "*This is Luard Dragonheart. If I'm not writing nor exploring the city, I also fly airships. I am already in the Wall of Wings as a trained pilot and trying to become an ace. I'd be happy to pilot for you.*"
He leaves to go to th <#863618958863237140>.
The full phrase now says "Kill the damn murder goose."

*Captain's Log, Day 4. This day has turned out quite shocking indeed. Early in the morning I ran across another follower of Athena, I must talk to her later about it. I'm quite sure that she is up to something here, maybe she is the clue I need to the visions my Goddess sent me, without her I also possibly couldn't have come closer to finding my Godmother's journal. After taking my leave of her I went to see an execution that was taking place to pray for the departed. To my shock it was the Frenchman who saved me earlier. Possibly on execution for my crimes. As it began a rescue party had begun, and to my shock the Frenchman was standing behind me, some other poor bloke was on the stand. He was hit by stray fire and the rescue party was trying to rescue the unconscious body. I did what I could to heal them so they might escape. I'm not a turn coat but I will not let an innocent man die with my intervention. If I see that Frenchman again I will have to interrogate him over what he has done.*

*Captians Log, Day 5. The city never seems to be without event. This morning I had decided to finally procure a weapon, as the dangers here have constantly increased I find myself in desperate need. I traveled to Central Park again to pray and Hark! she did call. There was a great battle that took place out of the pond. A great Gander, the one that it appears the pigeons had been warning us about. The battle was fierce and took several good warriors down, four to be exact. It was a dark time, but we were able to defeat the beast. And through the spoils I was able to claim some armour for myself as well as a greater weapon. I was also able to claim an alter and some food. I was shocked that the ones who had recruited the fight against it where the treasonous "patriots" But nonetheless the people are safe, and feel like I could take solace in that.  I also find myself rather conflicted recently. I was going through Hampstead and found an older Teifling man, He was carrying with him a rather unusual and large assortment of meat. He said his name was Malathor and he was from Transylvania, the memory of him still makes me unsettled. After helping him bring his groceries to the ordinary I ran into Secel, the follower of Athena I had mentioned prior, and a fellow called Bo. He asked us for our aide in delivering a package to a man called Count Kolro. I had agreed, although in hindsight I am unsure of whether or not I did the right thing. For one Secel seemed like something was bothering here the whole time, and because Secel was so nervous I never actually found out what I was delivering to the Count, all I know is that whatever it was we were rewarded handsomely for it. Which for many reasons has me more concerned. Along the way to deliver the crate we ran in Sabrine, the sargent? I had mentioned earlier as well, and a robotic fellow referred to as "Watcher". On our way through the sewers we were attacked by crocodiles and they were able to sneak up and bite the Watcher.*

*I'm glad the poor chap is alright but it was still quite treacherous. Afterwards Secel was even more unnerved and her, Sabrine, and I had a discussion about it. She is going through a rough time here and she is worried about her infernal heritage. In many ways I wonder if she is the reason why my goddess hath sent me here. We were able to calm here down and even get her to laugh, and my she has a wonderful laugh. I'm actually supposed to take her out for a meal sometime, get to know each-other better. I look forward to it, I'm thinking of something in Ferrytown. The relaxing atmosphere there might be good for the both of us. On another note I found out that the Frenchman that had caused all that trouble actually has passed on. If I'm being honest I know I shouldn't feel as upset as I do, He was a Frenchman and a traitor to the crown, but he still risked his life for me, and I don't think he should have died. I think all I really want is the fighting and death to stop.*

Johnathan watches as the bombs drop, the horrors of war he see's before him. Reminding him of all the battles he's seen, come once again to his homeland. For now he sits still

Johnathan begins to write a letter about the horrors he's seeing. The bombs dropping, the fireballs. The rampant destruction. The slaughter that is taking place all around him. He lowers his union jack to half mast, before he can't stand it anymore and takes the flag down all together.

*To the King
Even as I write the bombs still drop. The land and streets we once fought and died to save are being swatted at by our own hands. Innocents are shot down in the same lines as the criminals. The soldiers here harass and slaughter civilians all the while crying out "Bully for me, another one down, hail to the king." As I write the people are still dying, my tears streaming down on the paper. How will the people of this land ever come to sing "God save the King" if the crown is shown to be their demise. The shame I have felt for flying our proud flag has caused my to hide it from this abhorrent and reckless destruction. This night will be remembered by the rebels not as a deterrent from fighting but as a call to action, and from the ashes more will come, and the fighting will continue, and the death till will rise for us all. I beg of you to order a stop to this slaughter in your name, before the damage is irreparable. I beg of you

Former CPT Johnathan Wrask*
